findings.where: Hero, the contact row: the filled blue 'Write to me' box and the underlined address beside it (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The page's one real action doesn't work. 'Write to me' is drawn as a filled button and the address is underlined like a link, but the parts map says both are static, so clicking either does nothing. The only working mailto link is in the footer, at the bottom of a long page.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer who decides to contact Mark from the first screen. They click the button or the address, nothing happens, and they may decide the site is broken and leave.

findings.where: Hero, the 'Book a consultation' button next to 'Write to me' (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: There is a second filled blue button with the same weight as the first. It points to #consult, and the page has no consultation section for it to land on. So the first screen has two equal primary actions where the brief asks for one, and the one that works is a dead in-page jump. 'Book a consultation' also reads like a firm's sales funnel, not a personal advisor.
findings.who_objects: The visitor can't tell which button to use, and the one that works goes nowhere. The founder ruled 'one direct, personal way to reach him' and 'nothing salesy'.

findings.where: Hero margin notes (Istanbul 2025, Melbourne 2026, São Paulo 2024), plus the specimen section labels (Palette, Type, Texture, Article page, Motion, Tile notes)
findings.fault: The notes are set in the house blue, which the palette says is the link colour, and they name talks by title. They look like links to those talks, but the parts map says they are static. The section labels below the fold use the same false link colour. The brief asks for blue margin notes, so this is a clash between the brief and the rule that the link colour is kept for links. It goes to the founder.
findings.who_objects: A reader who wants the Istanbul or São Paulo talk. They click its title, nothing happens, and they have to look for it under Articles. The founder decides whether margin notes may keep the link blue.

findings.where: Hero ground: the pale blue-to-lilac gradient behind the heading, notes and photo
findings.fault: The hero sits on a cool lavender gradient, not the warm paper. That goes against the brief ('a warm paper ground', 'one soft ground', the house colours as the only ink). It also goes against the tile's own palette ('three colours, no accent') and texture ('No texture: the paper is a flat warm tone'). The gradient adds a colour outside the house blue and grey, puts a hard seam under the paper-coloured nav bar, and gives the first screen a slick, tech-product feel.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who asked for the house colours and a calm paper ground and judges this first screen first. A legal-journal direction looks like a SaaS landing page in exactly the place he looks.

findings.where: Hero, the first-person paragraph 'I ADVISE MULTILATERAL DEVELOPMENT BANKS…' (4 lines on desktop, 8 on phone)
findings.fault: Mark's personal introduction is set entirely in letter-spaced capitals. That is slow to read at this length. It also reads as a corporate label or a heading, not as a man speaking in the first person, and it is louder than the plain serif paragraph below it.
findings.who_objects: A reader skimming who Mark is and whom he advises, who has to decode a block of shouted capitals. The founder asked that Mark be heard in his own voice, and capitals make the sentence sound like a firm's tagline.

findings.where: Hero photograph and the repeated exhibit photo in the motion sketch
findings.fault: The candidate grades Mark's portrait to flat greyscale with a lifted, washed-out black. The result looks archival and lifeless, not 'real people in real light graded into the house colours'. With grey ink and the lilac ground around it, the first screen has no warm or living note.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who asked for 'alive, not boring' and for Mark's photograph to carry real weight. A grey, faded Mark is easy to read as a memorial or a past figure. (This is about the grade the tile applies, not the stand-in photo itself.)

findings.where: Phone hero, the action row under the São Paulo note
findings.fault: The two buttons and the address stack into a cramped pile. The address is squeezed between the buttons with almost no space, and 'Book a consultation' is indented from the left edge that everything else on the screen aligns to.
findings.who_objects: A phone visitor coming from a LinkedIn link can't tell whether the address belongs to the button above or the one below. The misaligned button looks like a layout mistake on a page meant to look carefully set.

findings.fault: The notes run Istanbul 2025, Melbourne 2026, São Paulo 2024, so they are neither newest-first nor in date order. The newest talk, Melbourne 2026, is not the first one a reader meets.
findings.who_objects: A procurement reader checking that Mark is current reads the dates as jumbled. The house's trust rule asks for the newest work to come first.

findings.fault: The exhibit photo and its table sit low in the right column while the curve fills the left. This leaves a large empty block under the curve and makes the section look unbalanced, as if two layouts were stacked out of step.
findings.who_objects: The founder reviewing the specimen: the sketch looks unfinished next to the evenly set palette and type sections above it.

findings.fault: A static photograph has a wide, soft resting drop shadow, so it looks lifted off the page like something you can pick up or click. Under the house rules, depth is only for things that float or can be acted on.
findings.who_objects: A visitor may try to click the photo to enlarge it or to open Mark's profile, and nothing happens.
